questions.question: __________ is the fraction 1/273.16 of the thermodynamic dynamic temperature of the triple point of water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelvin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kelvin is the base unit of temperature in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• It is defined as the fraction 1/273.16 of the thermodynamic temperature of the triple point of water.
 
• The triple point of water is the unique temperature and pressure at which water can coexist in equilibrium in all three phases: solid, liquid, and gas.
 
• The Kelvin scale does not use degrees; temperatures are simply stated in Kelvins (K).
 
• Absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature where molecular motion stops, is 0 K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermodynamic Temperature**

 
 
• It is a measure of the absolute energy of particles in a system.
 
• It is measured in Kelvins in the SI system.
 
 
 
• **Triple Point of Water**
 
 
• Occurs at precisely 273.16 K (0.01°C) and a pressure of 611.657 pascals.
 
• It is used to define the Kelvin unit in the SI system.
 
 
 
• **Absolute Zero**
 
 
• It is the theoretical lowest temperature possible, at which point particles have minimal vibrational motion.
 
• It is defined as 0 K, equivalent to -273.15°C or -459.67°F.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Scales**
 
 
• **Celsius (°C)**: Used in most parts of the world, based on the freezing (0°C) and boiling points (100°C) of water.
 
• **Fahrenheit (°F)**: Used primarily in the United States, where water freezes at 32°F and boils at 212°F.
 
• **Kelvin (K)**: Used in scientific contexts, based on absolute zero and the triple point of water.

questions.question: Distance of stars is measured in?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Light Year.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Light Year:**

 
• It is the **distance that a light photon travels in the vacuum in one Julian year. **
 
• A light-year is a **unit of distance.**
 
• **The value of one light-year is constant.**
 
• The term light-year is often used in astrophysics to measure the** distance between two astronomical objects. Hence, option 4 is correct.**
 
• Light travels at a **velocity of about 300,000 kilometres (km) per second.**
 
• It can travel about **10 trillion km. **
 
• More precisely, one light-year is equal to** 9,500,000,000,000 kilometres**.
 
 
• **One light-year, ly = 9.4607 × 10¹² km**
 
• **1 light-year in miles = 5.88 × 10¹² miles**
 
• **1 light-year in the Astronomical unit = 63241 au.**
 
 
 
• The Sun is at a distance of **149.6 million kilometres **away from earth.
 
 
• The same distance, when expressed in terms of the light-year approximates **15.54795 × 10⁻⁶ light years.**

questions.question: 25°C is equivalent to how many degrees on the Fahrenheit scale?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __77__ °__Fahrenheit.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Celsius is used in most of the world to calculate temperatures. At 0° Celsius, water freezes and boils at 100 °Celsius.
 
• Fahrenheit is a scale widely used in the United States for calculating temperatures.
 
• °Fahrenheit = {(9/5) x °Celsius} + 32 
 
• °Fahrenheit = (9/5) x 25 + 32
 
• °Fahrenheit = 45 + 32
 
• °Fahrenheit = 77°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• 80 °Fahrenheit = 26.67 °C
 
• 75 °Fahrenheit = 23.89 °C
 
• 87 °Fahrenheit = 30.56 °C

questions.question: Which of the following equations is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__**1 kW = 1000 Js⁻¹**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Power equivalent to 1Kw is 1000 watts or Js⁻¹.__
 
• A kilowatt is a unit of Electric Power.
 
• One Kilowatt is the energy consumption of 1000Joules/Second.
 
• Watts is represented as W and Kilowatt as Kw.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Electric power (P) is the rate at which work is done by the e.m.f. a source in maintaining current in the circuit. That is, 
 
• P= V. I = V2./R = I2. R 
 
• Electric Energy is the total work done by an e.m.f. a source in maintaining current in the circuit for a given time. Its SI unit is the joule (J) or (kWh).
 
• That is given by, 
 
• Electrical energy = Electrical power × time
 
 
• 1 unit = 1 kWh = Power (in kW) × time (hours).
 
 
 
• Calculation:__
 
 
• Given that, electrical energy = 1 kWh
 
• Where as 1 J = 1 Ws
 
• And
 
• 1 kW = 1000 W
 
• 1 h = 60×60 sec
 
• So, in terms of joule 1 kWh can be calculated as
 
• 1 kWh = 1 × 103× 60 × 60 = 3600 ×103 = 36 × 105 joule = 3.6 × 106 joule

questions.question: Which among the following is a unit of measurement that describes the rate at which the universe is expanding?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is **Hubble**** constant** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points:__

__
 
• 'Expanding Universe'

 
 
• Edwin Hubble, an American astronomer, was the first to prove that the universe is expanding.

questions.question: The boiling and freezing points of water are exactly ______ degrees apart on the Fahrenheit scale.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __180__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The boiling and freezing points of water are exactly 180 degrees apart on the Fahrenheit scale.
 
• The freezing point of water is 32°F on the Fahrenheit scale and the boiling point is 212°F (at standard atmospheric pressure).
 
• This puts 180 degrees apart from the boiling and freezing points of water. 
 
• Thus, a degree on the scale of Fahrenheit is 1⁄180 of the distance between the freezing point and the boiling point.
 
• The freezing and boiling points of water on the Celsius scale are 100 degrees apart.
 
 
• 1°F temperature interval is equal to a 5⁄9 degrees Celsius interval.
 
• At -40 ° (i.e. −40 °F = −40 °C), the Fahrenheit and Celsius scales converge.
 
 
 
• Absolute zero is -273.15 °C(-459.67 °F).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Boiling Point: 

 
 
• The boiling point is the temperature at which the vapour pressure of a liquid becomes equal to atmospheric pressure and it converts from liquid to a gaseous state.
 
• It is different at different altitudes.
 
• The boiling point of water under normal conditions is 100° C.
 
• The boiling point usually decreases at high altitudes. So at high altitudes, the boiling point of water is less than 100° C.

questions.question: The derived unit of the physical quantity, which is the product of mass and acceleration is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**newton**__.

__**Concept:**__

**Fundamental quantity**

__
 
• Fundamental quantities are physical quantities that are **not dependent on other physical quantities.**
 
• **Example:** length, mass, acceleration, time, current, luminous intensity, thermodynamic temperature, etc.

**Derived quantity**

 
• Derived quantity are those quantities **that are dependent on fundamental quantities.**
 
• **Example:** Area, volume, density, speed, force, velocity, etc.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• According to **Newton's second law of motion, force is defined or expressed as the product of mass and acceleration.**__
 
• Mathematically,** the force can be represented as:**
 
• **F = ma**
 
• where,
 
• F is the force applied.
 
• m is the mass of the body.
 
• a is the acceleration.
 
• The __**SI unit of force is the newton**__ which is represented by N.

Thus,__** the derived unit of the physical quantity, which is the product of mass and acceleration is newton.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**Some fundamental and derived quantities, along with their SI units, are listed in the table below.

questions.question: The SI unit of temperature is
questions.solution:
__Explanation__:

Celsius scale:

__
 
• In this scale, a lower fixed point (ice point) is taken 0° and the upper fixed point (steam point) is taken 100°.
 
• The temperature measured on this scale all in degree celsius (°C).

Fahrenheit scale:

 
• This scale of temperature has a lower fixed point at 32° F and an upper fixed point at 212° F.
 
• The change in temperature of 1° F corresponds to a change of less than 1° on the Celsius scale.

Kelvin scale:

 
• The Kelvin temperature scale is also known as the thermodynamic scale. The triple point of water is also selected to be the zero of the scale of temperature.
 
• The temperatures measured on this scale are in Kelvin (K).
 
• The S.I unit of temperature is Kelvin.__

__Note:__

__
 
• The Kelvin is the primary unit of temperature but is often used in conjunction with the Celsius degree, which has the same magnitude. Therefore option 1 is correct.
 
• The definition implies that absolute zero (0 K) is equivalent to −273.15 °C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**All these temperatures are related to each other by the following relationship:

frac{{F - 32}}{9} = (C)/(5) = frac{{K - 273}}{5}
